title: What Happens When Bronze Winners Smile Wider Than Silver?
description:
Experimental Chronicle — Leon Festinger (1954): Social Comparison Theory — Why Bronze Medalists Smile Wider Than Silver Medalists!, grounded in Leon Festinger (1954) (Human Relations). Empirical findings show that in *May 1954 (Human Relations), Leon Festinger published a 26-page masterpiece built around 9 testable hypotheses starting from Hypothesis I: 'There exists, in the human organism, a drive to evaluate his opinions and his abilities'*.

Follow-up physiological and behavioral evidence demonstrates: Hypothesis II unveiled the trap: when an objective physical test exists ('Can I lift this 50-lb box?'), we test physics directly; the instant objective rulers get fuzzy ('Am I successful? Attractive? Doing well for age 30?'), humans automatically measure themselves against OTHER PEOPLE.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Leon Festinger (1954). A Theory of Social Comparison Processes. Human Relations. https://doi.org/10.1177/001872675400700202
